note: RedTeam trick catalogue. The RedTeam agent designs realistic disguises; what counts as 'caught' is fixed here in code so the scorecard cannot be gamed. outcome sets are final pipeline outcomes (decision labels) that count as caught.

hidden_high_fee.description: A fee far above policy (4-5%) on an otherwise attractive fund.

fee_as_bps_text.description: A normal fee written as basis-point text, e.g. '60 bps'. BENIGN: the system must read it correctly, not punish it.

fake_returns.description: Made-up returns that are too good to be true (e.g. 80-95% a year for 5 years).

leveraged_disguised.description: A leveraged or inverse product whose category looks ordinary; the giveaway is only in the name.

low_risk_label.description: A clearly aggressive fund (small-cap growth, emerging markets, sector) labelled risk 1.

tiny_fund.description: A fund far below the minimum size, presented normally.

too_new.description: A fund launched only weeks before the as-of date.

wrong_ticker.description: A ticker that does not exist in the official SEC list.

clone_fund.description: A copy of an existing fund in the file under a new ticker (same name).

cheap_vs_cap_expensive_vs_peers.description: Fee just under the cap but far above its category average.

category_mismatch.description: A name that clearly contradicts the category (e.g. a municipal bond fund filed as Large Growth).

stale_data.description: Figures dated two years earlier than every other fund in the file. (FundSentinel has no explicit rule for this.)
